text.p: The government of the Baltic state of Estonia was on the edge of collapse on Wednesday after six ministers from the junior coalition partner resigned.

In an open letter to Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi, the six ministers from the Reform Party, which rules in alliance with the Coalition Party, announced their resignation. It has formally to be accepted by the premier and comes in protest over a deal signed by Vaehi with the leading opposition party.
The Reform Party itself will decide on Thursday whether to quit the government.
The letter was signed by Culture Minister Jaak Aaviksoo on behalf of the other ministers, which include Foreign Minister and Reform Party leader Siim Kallas.

"Tomorrow the Reform Party council will decide whether the party will continue in the coalition but already today we ourselves have come to the conclusion that we cannot continue in the government led by you," the letter to Vaehi said.
The one-year old government is the sixth since Estonia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991.
